apps.name: Portfolio Intelligence - Overview
apps.description: First-look Portfolio Intelligence dashboard on the synthetic demo account: sector X-Ray, a what-if trade preview, and one-year Brinson-Fachler attribution versus SPY. Group 1 links the what-if symbol; Group 2 links the account.
prompts: Which sectors dominate the demo book's X-Ray, and how concentrated is it?
What would buying 100 more shares of AAPL change in the demo book?
Explain the one-year Brinson-Fachler attribution versus SPY: which sectors added or lost active return, and was it allocation or selection?

apps.name: Portfolio Intelligence - Terminal
apps.description: Twelve-tab Portfolio Intelligence terminal. It starts on a sample (demo) account and sample data until you connect your own. Research tabs F1-F7 follow the symbol in Group 1; portfolio tabs F8-F11 and Morning Review follow the account in Group 2. Every tab shows where its data comes from and whether the data providers are healthy. The suggested prompts walk a ten-step weekly review: provider health and company profile, financials, sector X-Ray, risk and attribution, upcoming events, alerts, paper trading, the morning review and analyst views of a sample basket.
prompts: Weekly review, step 1 of 10 (F1: Overview > Provider Health Table): Are all my data providers healthy, or is anything showing sample data before I start my weekly review?
Weekly review, step 2 of 10 (F1: Overview > Equity Profile - Header + Live Price): What does AAPL do, and where is its price trading right now?
Weekly review, step 3 of 10 (F2: Financials > Equity Profile - Financial Statement Charts): How have AAPL's revenue, net income and net margin trended over the last five years?
Weekly review, step 4 of 10 (F8: X-Ray > X-Ray - Sector Weights): How is my portfolio split across sectors?
Weekly review, step 5 of 10 (F9: Risk & Attribution > Risk Dashboard): How risky is my portfolio right now, and what drove its return versus the benchmark?
Weekly review, step 6 of 10 (F6: Calendar > Event Calendar): Which earnings, dividends or filings are coming up for my holdings?
Weekly review, step 7 of 10 (F11: Alerts & Catalysts > Alerts Panel): Which alerts and smart-money moves need my attention?
Weekly review, step 8 of 10 (F10: Paper Trading > Paper Performance KPIs (PAPER)): How is my paper trading account doing on return, Sharpe ratio and drawdown?
Weekly review, step 9 of 10 (Morning Review (W8) > Alerts Panel): Can you give me a one-page morning review of my portfolio: risk, paper performance, upcoming events and alerts?
Weekly review, step 10 of 10 (F7: Estimates > Basket Analyst Consensus): What do analysts think of the stocks in my basket? (This view uses a sample basket for now.)
Summarize AAPL from the research tabs: fundamentals, technicals, peers and analyst estimates.
Review the demo book's concentration, risk and upcoming catalysts, and list the three items that need attention this week.

apps.name: Techtrade Trading Desk
apps.description: Systematic-trader desk over persisted TechTrade artifacts: Morning Scan (T1), Position Workbench (T2), Validation (T3), Tuning (T4), Engine Status (T5) and Audit Journal (T6). Group 1 links the symbol across the scan table, workbench, validation, tuning and audit. Calculation, validation, approval and paper artifacts stay separate; the Execute Bridge only reports readiness and places no orders.
prompts: Which segments have the strongest signals in this morning's scan, and which symbols should I look at first?
Walk me through the AAPL signal, trading plan and order legs, including the stop, target and reward-to-risk.
Did the AAPL strategy pass validation? Explain the PBO, deflated Sharpe and out-of-sample Sharpe behind the verdict.
Compare AAPL's validated replay returns with its realized forward simulation in the audit journal.
